title: Mergers & Acquisitions
completion_message: ¡Excelente! El mundo de 'M&A' (Fusiones y Adquisiciones) es donde se cierran los tratos más grandes del planeta. Ya tienes el vocabulario para entender cómo los titanes corporativos devoran o se unen a sus rivales.

parts.visual:
El término 'M&A' (Mergers and Acquisitions) domina las noticias financieras. 

1. Synergy (Sinergia): 
- El concepto de que dos empresas juntas valen más que separadas (1+1=3). 
Ej: The merger will create massive SYNERGIES in marketing and distribution. 

2. Takeover bid (Oferta pública de adquisición / OPA): 
- Una oferta formal para comprar las acciones de una empresa y tomar el control. 
Ej: Microsoft launched a $40 billion TAKEOVER BID for the tech company. 

3. Spin-off (Escisión / Empresa derivada): 
- Cuando una empresa separa una de sus divisiones para crear una nueva compañía independiente. 
Ej: The corporation decided to SPIN OFF its healthcare division.
parts.audio: Welcome to Mergers and Acquisitions, commonly known as M&A. This is where the biggest deals on the planet happen. Number 1: Synergy. The concept that the value of two companies combined will be greater than the sum of their separate parts. One plus one equals three. For example: The merger will create massive SYNERGIES in marketing and distribution. Number 2: Takeover bid. A type of corporate action in which a company makes an offer to purchase another company. For example: Microsoft launched a 40 billion dollar TAKEOVER BID for the tech company. Number 3: Spin-off. When a company creates a new independent business by selling or distributing new shares of an existing business division. For example: The corporation decided to SPIN OFF its healthcare division.

parts.visual:
4. Monopoly (Monopolio): 
- Cuando una sola empresa domina todo un mercado. 
Ej: If they buy their only competitor, they will have a MONOPOLY. 

5. Antitrust laws (Leyes antimonopolio): 
- Leyes diseñadas para promover la competencia y evitar monopolios. 
Ej: The merger was blocked by ANTITRUST regulators. 

6. Golden parachute (Paracaídas dorado): 
- Una cláusula que garantiza un pago millonario a un ejecutivo si la empresa es comprada y él es despedido. 
Ej: The CEO left with a $20 million GOLDEN PARACHUTE. 

7. Due diligence (Debida diligencia / Auditoría previa): 
- La investigación financiera y legal profunda antes de comprar una empresa. 
Ej: During DUE DILIGENCE, we discovered massive hidden debts.
parts.audio: Number 4: Monopoly. When a single company or group owns all or nearly all of the market for a given type of product or service. For example: If they buy their only competitor, they will have a MONOPOLY. Number 5: Antitrust laws. These are regulations that encourage competition by limiting the market power of any particular firm. For example: The merger was blocked by ANTITRUST regulators. Number 6: Golden parachute. A huge severance package guaranteed to a top executive if they lose their job due to a merger or takeover. For example: The CEO left with a 20 million dollar GOLDEN PARACHUTE. Number 7: Due diligence. An exhaustive investigation of a business before signing a contract. For example: During DUE DILIGENCE, we discovered massive hidden debts.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige el término de M&A correcto.

questions.question: The combination of the two companies is expected to create massive cost ____, saving millions every year. (Sinergias).
questions.explanation: Synergies = sinergias (el valor conjunto es mayor).

questions.question: The larger company made a hostile takeover ____ to buy all outstanding shares at $50 each. (Oferta de adquisición).
questions.explanation: Takeover bid = oferta de adquisición / OPA.

questions.question: To focus on its core software business, the corporation decided to ____ off its hardware division into a new company. (Escindir / Separar).
questions.explanation: Spin-off = escisión corporativa (crear una empresa a partir de una división).

questions.question: The government blocked the merger because it would create a ____, killing all competition in the market. (Monopolio).
To prevent monopolies, the government enforces strict ____ laws. (Leyes antimonopolio).
questions.explanation: Antitrust laws = leyes antimonopolio (en EE.UU. y Europa).

questions.question: The CEO didn't mind being fired after the acquisition because he had a $15 million golden ____. (Indemnización millonaria).
questions.explanation: Golden parachute = paracaídas dorado (indemnización masiva por despido en M&A).

questions.question: Before we finalize the purchase, our legal and financial teams must spend a month performing due ____. (Auditoría / Investigación exhaustiva).
When two companies of roughly equal size agree to join forces and become a single new company, it's called a ____. (Fusión).
questions.explanation: Merger = fusión (a menudo entre iguales o mutuo acuerdo).

questions.question: When a larger company buys a smaller company and absorbs it, it's called an ____. (Adquisición).
questions.explanation: Acquisition = adquisición (una empresa compra a otra).

questions.question: M&A stands for ____ and Acquisitions.
questions.explanation: M&A = Mergers and Acquisitions (Fusiones y Adquisiciones).

questions.question: To defend against the hostile takeover, the board swallowed a 'poison ____', creating new shares to dilute the attacker's power.
questions.explanation: Poison pill = píldora envenenada (estrategia defensiva financiera).

questions.question: A wealthy individual or company that rescues a target company from a hostile takeover is called a 'white ____'.
questions.explanation: White knight = caballero blanco (un comprador amistoso que salva a la empresa de un comprador hostil).

questions.question: The process of integrating two companies after a merger is extremely difficult due to clashing corporate ____. (Culturas).
questions.explanation: Corporate culture clash = choque de culturas corporativas (el mayor problema en M&A).

questions.question: If a company wants to buy another, the first official step is usually to sign a Letter of ____ (LOI). (Carta de intención).
questions.explanation: Letter of Intent (LOI) = Carta de intención.

questions.question: The company being targeted for acquisition is known as the ____ company. (Objetivo).
questions.explanation: Target company = la empresa objetivo (la que va a ser comprada).

questions.question: To buy the competitor, they used borrowed money (debt). This is called a ____ buyout (LBO). (Compra apalancada).
questions.explanation: Leveraged Buyout (LBO) = compra financiada con deuda (apalancada).

questions.question: A company that buys other companies purely as investments, without producing anything itself, is a ____ company. (Sociedad gestora / matriz).
questions.explanation: Holding company = sociedad tenedora o matriz.

questions.question: When a company buys one of its suppliers to control the supply chain, it's called ____ integration. (Integración vertical).
questions.explanation: Vertical integration = comprar proveedores o distribuidores.

questions.question: When a company buys a direct competitor to increase market share, it's called ____ integration. (Integración horizontal).
questions.explanation: Horizontal integration = comprar a un competidor directo.

questions.question: The difference between the purchase price and the actual book value of the acquired company's assets is recorded as ____. (Fondo de comercio / Prestigio).
questions.explanation: Goodwill = fondo de comercio (el valor intangible por el que se paga de más, como la marca o los clientes).
